ui.chat.thread_search.building.role: status line in the find overlay
ui.chat.thread_search.building.note: The index is still being built for this conversation, so the panel has no answer yet; it is a wait, not a failure. Recoverable by itself.

ui.chat.thread_search.building_hint.role: hint appended to the building status line
ui.chat.thread_search.building_hint.note: Follows the building sentence in dimmed text and says WHY waiting helps: the panel re-asks once and the index's own result arrives. Never a call to action — the reader does nothing.

ui.chat.thread_search.close_label.note: Closes the find overlay only; the conversation and its transcript stay open behind it. The visible glyph is an X with no text.

ui.chat.thread_search.count.match.note: How many messages matched, when every hit is an exact occurrence of the query. The count is of MESSAGES, not occurrences, and the backend caps the list — the truncation note rides beside it rather than inside it.

placeholders.countText: Already-formatted decimal count from String(count); separate from the ICU cardinal so English does not gain thousands separators.

ui.chat.thread_search.count.match.plural_guidance: English one/other is source grammar, not a target-locale limit. Use the target locale's native categories (Russian few/many, Arabic zero/two) as the locale's style guide requires.

ui.chat.thread_search.count.related.note: All hits are RELATED matches: the index matched the sense of the query, not its literal characters, so none of the rows highlights the typed words. The word `related` must stay distinct from the plain match count.

placeholders.countText: Already-formatted decimal count from String(count); see the plain match count.

ui.chat.thread_search.count.related.plural_guidance: As the plain match count: follow the target locale's own plural categories.

ui.chat.thread_search.count.split.note: The only line that states the exact/related split: two counts separated by a middot. It exists because a bare total hid that most hits were only related. Keep the separator glyph and the two qualifiers.

ui.chat.thread_search.count.truncated.role: suffix under a capped result list
ui.chat.thread_search.count.truncated.note: Says the list is a FLOOR, not a total: the backend returned the first N hits. Stays parenthesised because it follows the count line as a suffix. Reads `the first match shown` in the singular case.
ui.chat.thread_search.count.truncated.length: Three or four words in parentheses.

placeholders.count: Cardinal number of hits the list shows.
placeholders.countText: Already-formatted decimal count from String(count); see the plain match count.

ui.chat.thread_search.empty.role: status line in the find overlay
ui.chat.thread_search.empty.note: The search finished and nothing matched. Not an error and not a suggestion: the reader knows what to edit, and the box is still focused.

ui.chat.thread_search.error.role: status line in the find overlay
ui.chat.thread_search.error.note: The find request itself failed (the transcript is fine). A separate `Try again` control sits beside this line; do not put the retry instruction in this sentence.

ui.chat.thread_search.hint.browse.note: Stands beside the arrow keys in the panel footer, so it stays lowercase.

ui.chat.thread_search.hint.close.note: Stands beside Esc in the panel footer, so it stays lowercase.

ui.chat.thread_search.hint.jump.note: Stands beside Enter in the panel footer, so it stays lowercase.

ui.chat.thread_search.jumping.role: status line under the result list
ui.chat.thread_search.jumping.note: Shown while a far hit is being sought in the transcript; a reach can take seconds, and the trailing ellipsis is what says the wait is still running. The transcript reports the landing itself.

ui.chat.thread_search.list_label.note: The accessible name of the listbox holding the hits. Not a heading and never rendered visually.

ui.chat.thread_search.partial.role: status line in the find overlay
ui.chat.thread_search.partial.note: The index is still catching up and the answer it gave may be incomplete. Softer than the building sentence: the list IS shown, with a caveat, so do not imply the search failed.

ui.chat.thread_search.placeholder.role: search field placeholder and accessible name
ui.chat.thread_search.placeholder.note: Both the placeholder inside the empty box and the combobox's accessible name, and the scope word matters: it searches the OPEN conversation, never the app, the files or other chats.

ui.chat.thread_search.recheck.note: Re-asks a conversation whose index was still building. Nothing failed, so this is a re-check rather than a retry, and the label must not imply an error.

ui.chat.thread_search.role.agent.role: message author label on a result row
ui.chat.thread_search.role.agent.note: The message was written by the agent. Humanised on purpose: the wire value `agent` stays out of the UI. Sits before a middot and the tier hint on a related row.

ui.chat.thread_search.role.user.role: message author label on a result row
ui.chat.thread_search.role.user.note: The message is the reader's own; `You` rather than `User` because the transcript calls the reader's message theirs too. Sits before a middot and the tier hint on a related row.

ui.chat.thread_search.searching.role: status line in the find overlay
ui.chat.thread_search.searching.note: A request is in flight and there is no earlier result list to show. The trailing ellipsis is the only thing saying the wait continues, so keep it.

ui.chat.thread_search.stale.role: status line above a retained result list
ui.chat.thread_search.stale.note: A new query's answer is in flight and the rows below are still the PREVIOUS query's — actionable, but not this query's answer. It replaced a count line that read as the current total. Keep the dash and the possessive.

ui.chat.thread_search.tier.related.role: match-kind hint on a result row
ui.chat.thread_search.tier.related.note: Follows a middot after the author label on a hit that matched the query's sense, not its characters. Lowercase because it continues the row's meta line, and `related` must stay the same word as in the related count line.

ui.chat.thread_search.unsupported.role: status line in the find overlay
ui.chat.thread_search.unsupported.note: The conversation's messages live on another device, so this client cannot search them at all. Nothing the reader can do here — do not offer a retry.
